Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spike since new model variant

Hi Avery —

We started seeing large p95/p99 latency spikes and increased 5xx error rates on our triage endpoints around 08:50 PDT this morning. We noticed the traffic was routed to the new model variant labeled apex-v3.1-rc during your canary — p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s and p99 is often >4s. Throughput looks steady but user-facing timeouts started occurring.

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike since new model variant

Quick triage notes (preliminary):
- Observed a sharp increase in tail latencies concentrated on a subset of serving nodes (host pool us-west-2-stable-07).
- Error spike correlates with KV cache misses for longer sequence inputs. The new apex-v3.1-rc build introduced a quantized kernel path that, under certain sequence-length distributions (>512 tokens), falls back to a slower CPU path for attention computations. That fallback is causing token-level delays cascaded across batch scheduling, which amplifies p95/p99.
- We see increased kernel execution times and context switch activity on those hosts.

Immediate recommendations:
- Rollback the canary (stop apex-v3.1-rc) OR route ApexHealth traffic to fallback model variant apex-v3.0-stable for the next 2 hours while we patch.
- Increase instance concurrency on the affected pool to reduce scheduling pressure if routing/fallback isn't instantaneous.

I'm collecting perf traces and will attach them in a minute. Also linking our rollback runbook for reference: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-rollout-fallback

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 18:30:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: ApexHealth: urgent — model rollout performance surge impacting triage (mitigation summary)

Update and summary of mitigation (post-triage):
- Action taken: canary apex-v3.1-rc was rolled back at 16:40 PDT on 2028-04-04 after we confirmed routing could move to apex-v3.0-stable without loss of model fidelity for your workload.
- Immediate effect: p95 returned to baseline (~240ms) and p99 reduced to <650ms within 30 minutes; error rates normalized.
- Root cause (prelim): a quantized attention kernel introduced in the new build did not correctly optimize for mid-long contexts. For sequences >512 tokens the runtime triggered a CPU fallback path; this led to CPU contention and batch scheduling delays on the affected host pool.
- Remediation plan: engineering will revert the quantized kernel change in the 3.1 branch and push a guarded feature flag with gradual traffic ramp and extended sequence-length unit tests (target: PR #4821). We'll also add a pre-rollout check for kernel fallback behaviors to the canary checklist.

Next steps for Customer/Commercial:
- Marissa/Ben to send the customer-facing note with apology and credit offer.
- I'll prepare a short postmortem draft and schedule a follow-up runbook update.
- Offer: 30-min exec briefing this week — please propose times.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md, rollback-audit.log

Thanks everyone — apologies for the disruption, and we'll follow up with the postmortem and timeline for the patch.

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
